newsitem.title: CANADA: Caledonia finds copper-gold Zambia deposit.
newsitem.headline: Caledonia finds copper-gold Zambia deposit.

text.p: Caledonia Mining Corp said on Friday it found a copper-gold deposit located west of Kapiri Mposhi in its Kadola license area in Zambia.

Caledonia senior geologist Tim Warman said an incomplete drilling program in December 1995 at the deposit, called Eureka, intersected copper grading 0.53 to 3.26 percent copper and gold grading from 0.25 to 2.18 grams of gold per tonne. Intersection widths ranged from 26 to 78 metres.
"That was just a very quick look," Warman said. "We did some soil sampling over the area and picked up a very strong soil geochemical anomoly with copper and also with bismuth."
Warman said that Caledonia also completed geophysic testing over the area, which was still being interpreted.

He said Caledonia was continuing soil samples at the Kadola license area, located in what he called the southern extension of the Copperbelt. The Kadola area comprises the Kadola West copper-cobalt deposit, the Eureka copper-gold deposit and an early-stage cobalt oxide deposit called Bopalo.

Caledonia's previously announced drill results from the Kadola West deposit found 12 of 15 holes intersecting copper and cobalt oxide mineralization in widths from three to 29 metres, grading 0.62 to 2.57 percent copper.

Warman said in a telephone interview that the company's drilling program was currently confined to its Nama copper-cobalt discovery area northwest of the Copperbelt. Recent calculations boosted the indicated and inferred mineral resource at Nama to more than 300 million tonnes grading 0.030 percent at a cutoff of 0.015 percent.
Warman said future drilling at Kadola depended on equipment supply and was hampered by the rainy season.
